Definition: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame:--tame.
BiblicalUsage: To tame is what man does to every kind of beast and bird and serpent, and James says the one thing no man can tame is the tongue. The wild horse is broken, the demon-possessed man could not be bound with chains, yet the tongue runs loose in every gathering. The contrast is the point: we have mastered the creatures and failed to master ourselves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the untamed tongue is the proof of our need for grace. Only the Spirit can bridle what no man can tame, and the tongue is where that work shows first.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
